quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home with a friend who hasn't been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a friend who hasn't been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid driving impaired is to arrange a ride with a sober friend. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your blood. Your body takes about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.
Stop wherever you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull over to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: It is best to keep space around your vehicle:

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front.
On all sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides.
questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol level.
Stops the effects of alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.
Raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. It may help you stay awake, but it cannot make you sober or reduce the alcohol in your blood.

questions.question: Increase your following distance when:

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
Exiting the highway.
Following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting the highway, and when behind motorcycles or bicycles.

questions.question: You can avoid alcohol-related crashes by:

options.text: Deciding before you start drinking that you will not drive.
Saying "No thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.
Calling a taxi.
Doing any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doing any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices later.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must do. This sign means parking is not allowed.

questions.question: If you drive a heavy truck or bus on the highway, you:

options.text: Must be careful of other drivers and pedestrians.
Can use your vehicle's size to your advantage in traffic.
Can expect smaller vehicles to stay out of your way.
Are responsible only for your truck and its cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be careful of other drivers and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses can cause serious damage in an accident. Drivers of these vehicles must understand their vehicle's limits and be responsible for protecting other drivers, passengers, and cargo.

questions.question: A bicyclist who doesn't obey traffic laws:

options.text: Is allowed to because bicyclists don't have to obey traffic laws.
Can be ticketed.
Will always get a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: You are waiting at a stop sign in a line of vehicles. After the vehicles ahead pass through with no cross traffic, you:

options.text: May go through without stopping again.
Must stop at the stop sign before proceeding.
May slowly roll past the stop sign.
May follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop at the stop sign before proceeding.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not let other traffic pressure you to skip this step.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the road shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, slow down without braking hard. Then carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic before re-entering the road.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive slower than other traffic.
Drive at the same speed as other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Drive at the same speed as the traffic around you, as long as you stay within the posted speed limit.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to share half a lane.
Share the same lane when passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle and needs a complete lane, just like any other vehicle. Even if there seems to be room to share a lane, motorcycles need space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull all the way off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the gas pedal, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, don't panic. Release the gas pedal and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road with both hands on the wheel. Use a small steering turn to get back into the right lane. Check for traffic before moving back onto the pavement.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, you should use ____ to show you are turning.

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers you are turning.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, the first thing you should do is:

options.text: Press your brakes hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Use your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: To slow down on a slippery road, first take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with slow, steady pressure.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles usually go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
More than 12 inches from the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the road's edge.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
Only if the car ahead is going under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no traffic can cross them, except when turning into a driveway or business entrance. You cannot pass another car by crossing double yellow lines.

questions.question: You notice your vehicle has a defect that may affect safe operation. You should:

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you have money.
Drive slower than usual.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that affects safe operation must be fixed right away. Do not drive the vehicle until the defect is repaired.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must make many decisions while driving. Any extra task can distract you and create danger. Keep your full attention on the road.

questions.question: A bus signals to rejoin the road after stopping. What must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a bus rejoining the main road after it stops. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus safely enter traffic.

questions.question: Why should you use extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane?

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. Slow down, yield, and be ready to stop. Protect the pedestrian from danger.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way with which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green left arrow means you can turn in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop, if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop and check that the way is clear before you go.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you should:

options.text: Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.
Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing, return to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway must:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: Drivers entering from a driveway must yield to cars already on the road. Merge safely when it is clear.

questions.question: A driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing with no traffic light. Who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last
The driver
Whoever is slower
The pedestrian

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection, even without a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area
The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limits show the fastest and slowest speeds allowed. These limits are for good conditions. You must slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive as you would on dry roads.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, stay farther back from other cars. It takes longer to stop when roads are wet or icy.
